text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Cabinet ministers say construction at Ras al-Amoud will harm Har Homa project.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu demands Treasury prepare new outlook forecasting growth in 1998.
- Attorney-general says cabinet ministers who vote against government decision in parliament effectively resign.
- 16-year-old Bedouin girl who stabbed her husband will not go to jail.
JERUSALEM POST
- Poll finds settlers more defiant on leaving settlements.
- Appeal filed vs. Ras al-Amoud. Netanyahu says bad time to build.
- U.S. envoy Dennis Ross expected here in two weeks with new plan.
- Gaon presents Koor's plans to Claridge.
- Siemens in talks to buy stake in two Israeli firms.
- Israel, Hungary agree free-trade pact.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Shin Bet warnings against Ras al-Amoud construction will help block project.
- The three victims of Maccabiah bridge collapse died from swallowing river toxins.
- Police have a list of public figures who bought academic papers in order to obtain university degrees.
MAARIV
- Most rivers in Israel are at least as toxic as Yarkon where Maccabiah bridge collapsed.
- Memorial for fallen Druze army officer wrecked.
GLOBES
- Netanyahu to hoteliers: "Even with a prime minster's salary, hotel rates are unaffordable."
- Prime minister's economic adviser: "Legislating Bank of Israel law delayed with appointment of new finance minister."
- No change expected in Bank of Israel's interest rate announcement.
